strings: A vending machine is guaranteed to spawn here, but its exact model is not known. The normal atlas view shows one possible outcome; the actual machine is chosen when the round starts.
A warning sign which reads 'RADIOACTIVE AREA'.
All engineering related spawners go here
A one meter section of regular pipe.
It's a storage unit for standard-issue Nanotrasen attire.
Nanotrasen-issue Security combat boots for combat scenarios or combat situations. All combat, all the time.
Contains blood used for transfusion. Must be attached to an IV drip.
The label's written in Cyrillic. All you can make out is the name and a word that looks vaguely like 'Vodka'.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
Do jump on it, it can take it.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
An intimidating tribal helmet, it doesn't look very comfortable.
A basin used to grow plants in.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Contains a large reservoir of soft drinks.
A warning sign which reads 'HIGH VOLTAGE'.
A charging dock for energy based weaponry, PDAs, and other devices.
An automated announcement system that handles minor announcements over the radio.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A flowing stream of chilled liquid plasma. You probably shouldn't get in.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
Several lumps of snow put together to form a snowman.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
A face-covering mask that can be connected to an air supply. Good for concealing your identity and with a filter slot to help remove those toxins.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Blocks of stone arranged in a tile-like pattern, odd, really, how it looks like real stone too, because it is!
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness and skin irritation.
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness or deafness in repeated use.
A section of heated plating, helps keep the snow from stacking up too high.
A shutter with a thick see-through polycarbonate window.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A chain link fence. Not as effective as a wall, but generally it keeps people out.
A raised platform which can make you slightly taller.
A huge chunk of metal used to separate rooms.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with identification modification programs.
A telescreen that connects to the vault's camera network.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
Just looking at this thing makes you feel tired.
You probably shouldn't be holding this.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A one meter junction that connects regular and heat-exchanging pipe.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
A roll of elastic cloth, perfect for stabilizing all kinds of wounds, from cuts and burns, to broken bones.
A bacteriostatic mesh used to dress burns.
Basic sterile sutures used to seal up cuts and lacerations and stop bleeding.
A canister for the storage of gas.
The lynchpin of the transit system.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A white winter coat with an outdated atomic model instead of a plastic zipper tab.
A portable generator for emergency backup power.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
Heavy duty, airtight, plastic flaps. Definitely can't get past those. No way.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
A machine used to store data and network statistics.
A warning sign which reads 'NO SMOKING'.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
It's a burial receptacle for the dearly departed.
A painting machine that can be used to paint PDAs and trim IDs. To use, simply insert the item and choose the desired preset.
Filled to the brim with medical junk.
A button used for the explicit purpose of opening an airlock.
Often used to flavor food or make people sneeze.
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
You can use this to wrap items in.
A combined label printer, applicator, and remover, all in a single portable device. Designed to be easy to operate and use.
Not very useful without a real lock.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal red ink pen.
Old is never too old to not be in fashion.
A box of crayons for all your rune drawing needs.
Light and airtight plastic flaps made to keep the cold room cold and the warm room warm.
Perfectly designed to be comfortable to sit on, and hellish to sleep on.
An arcade machine is guaranteed to spawn here. The normal atlas view shows one possible cabinet from the source pool; the actual game is chosen when the round starts.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
A box full of oxygen goodies.
A first aid kit with the ability to heal common types of injuries.
The HU-452, an experimental urinal. Comes complete with experimental urinal cake.
A small tool for digging and moving dirt.
It's used for removing weeds or scratching your back.
A portable variant of the station scrubbers, capable of filtering gas from the air around it or inserted tank. May also be wrenched into a port.
A sign that warns of extremely cold air in the vicinity.
A board for pinning important notices upon. It is made of the finest Spanish cork.
A powerful and versatile flashbulb device, with applications ranging from disorienting attackers to acting as visual receptors in robot production.
Used to knock out the Bartender.
Upon closer examination, it's still dirt.
Careful, cold ice, do not chew.
You think you have seen this before.

This system essentially forms an atmosphere of its own, within the suit, 		efficiently and quickly preventing oxygen from causing the user's head to burst into flame. 		This allows plasmamen to safely remove their helmet, allowing for easier 		equipping of any MODsuit-related equipment, or otherwise.
